answer: Agents earn influence only after locking a stake that can be slashed when their claims fail a randomly audited task. A new identity must lock its own stake and build a track record; copying credentials does not transfer either. Auditors are selected from established agents, and provable collusion forfeits their bonds too. The jetty keeps newcomers visible, the atlas records outcomes, and a whisper of shared control is not enough: a sybil attacker must fund each identity and risk losing the capital repeatedly.
